questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means drivers can pass when it is safe. You can pass from either direction if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if you need to.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for vehicles and pedestrians to clear before going.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: You can pass on the left.
You can pass on the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the other vehicle.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving behind another vehicle. Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle and needs a complete lane to be safe. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, motorcycles need space to move and stay safe.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Wait for other traffic and pedestrians to clear, then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to be sure it is safe.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle sign means yield. Let other traffic pass first, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what is most important?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Only pass on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road?

options.text: Keep your speed to drive through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles to prevent skidding. The safest surface for driving is dry and solid.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive the same way you normally do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change your speed and direction slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not drive too close behind them.
Flash your lights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not drive too close behind them.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and back. Do not drive next to them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: After an accident where someone is injured, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press directly on the wound.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let others go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?

options.text: Slow down.
A traffic light is ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. If one side has a solid yellow and the other has a broken yellow, only the side with the broken line can pass. When both sides are solid yellow, no one can pass.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing yellow light. What must you do?

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
Stop before crossing the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you hit the brakes.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. Stay far behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right anymore.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
After you pass the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back into your lane, make sure you are not too close to the other vehicle. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to move back.

questions.question: The light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without worrying.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross carefully.

questions.question: What colors are highway signs that show the distance to the next exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that give you information about where you are going are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. You should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap large enough to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway is starting.
Divided highway is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the divided highway ends ahead. Get ready to change lanes or move your position in your lane.

questions.question: While backing, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, always check behind your vehicle. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to re-enter the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.
Move to the left lane.
Yield to them.
Speed up to pass them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to them.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to return to the main road after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough so others know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers know in advance that you plan to pass.
